podcast.body: Collaborated with Thomas Dorsey (as Georgia Tom) on this seminal hocombe record, which sold seven million copies and significantly influenced blues and R&B music. "he'd collaborated with Tampa Red on a series of singles. Their song It's Tight Like That from 1928 is one of the earliest hocombe records, and is largely responsible for a lot of the cliches of the form, and it sold seven million copies."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 5: "This Train" by Sister Rosetta Tharpe

podcast.body: This early blues recording, made in 1928 by Tampa Red and Georgia Tom, featured very suggestive titles and lyrics. It contributed to the outrage of the time over "dirty lyrics" appearing in new music technology. "Like you've got to give me some. Shake that thing, and it's tight like that by Tampa Red and Georgia Tom in 1928."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
